sections.h2: Fort Collins housing at a glance
sections.html:
Fort Collins is the Larimer County seat, roughly 60 miles north of Denver, and it counted 169,810 residents in 2020, which made it the fourth largest city in Colorado. The wider county had a 2025 estimate of 377,292 people and 158,769 housing units, with 63.8% of occupied homes owned by the people living in them.

Homes near the Cache la Poudre River or Spring Creek can draw flood questions from buyers and lenders. The city's worst flood hit in late July 1997, and sellers in those areas should expect the topic to come up in a showing or an inspection.

Your city does not bill property tax. The Larimer County Treasurer mails the statement, collects payment and sends the money out to every taxing authority on your bill, including the school district, the city and any special districts. The Treasurer has no say in how much you owe.

  • Questions about value or how the tax was figured go to the Larimer County Assessor.
  • Payments, statements, delinquent balances and the lien sale go to the Treasurer and Public Trustee.
  • Once a mortgage is paid off and the lender stops paying your tax, the Treasurer's site explains how to get your own statement.

The Public Trustee side of the same office handles foreclosures and the release of deeds of trust under Title 38 of the Colorado Revised Statutes. That is the office that matters when an old loan still sits on the record.

Taxes are due on January 1 for the previous year, and you can pay in one of two ways. Partial payments are not accepted. A due date on a non-business day moves to the next business day.

Payment optionDue dateNotes
First halfEnd of FebruaryTwo equal installments
Second halfJune 15Pairs with the February payment
Full paymentApril 30One payment instead of two

If you sell mid-year, ask the closing company how the current year's share will be handled, because the bill in hand covers the year before.

The annual sale of tax liens on unpaid real estate is set for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026. It takes place at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch, 5280 Arena Circle, Loveland, in the Thomas McKee 4-H Community Building.

A Fort Collins owner with delinquent real estate tax should phone the Treasurer before that date. Investors who want to bid find their own information on the same site, so the sale draws from two sides: owners trying to clear a balance and buyers hunting for liens.

sections.h2: Online tools and other ways to pay
sections.html:
The Treasurer takes payment online, issues receipts, and offers eNotices and email reminders. For automated monthly payments, the office signed up with EquaPay by Autoagent, formerly EscrowTaxes. Any Larimer County property without mortgage escrow can use it.

  • Title companies sign in separately to order Certificates of Taxes Due.
  • Mortgage companies have a mass payment option.
  • Owners can change a mailing address, search property and tax records, and print a receipt.
  • Manufactured homes, business personal property and special assessments each have their own pages.

Payment and search pages are sometimes offline for maintenance, so do not leave a deadline payment to the last minute.

Public schools in Fort Collins run through the Poudre School District, which also levies tax on your bill. The school boundary a house sits in is therefore part of its tax area, and it is worth confirming which districts apply before you quote any bill to a buyer. A buyer comparing two houses will often ask which district each one falls in, and the Larimer County Assessor can sort out which taxing authorities apply to a parcel.

sections.h2: What to do about taxes when you sell
sections.html:
An unpaid balance does not stop a sale, but it has to be dealt with before the deed changes hands. Here is the order that works for most sellers.

  1. Tell your title company early so it can order the Certificate of Taxes Due through the Treasurer's title login.
  2. Read the certificate for any prior year balance or lien.
  3. If the account is delinquent and the lien sale is close, call the Treasurer before the sale date.
  4. Pay the balance from your proceeds at closing.
  5. If a loan is being paid off, confirm the Public Trustee has what it needs to release the deed of trust.

A cash buyer goes through the same title steps. What you skip is the lender's appraisal and repair demands, which helps when a house is dated or needs work. Cash does not erase a tax lien or a deed of trust, though. Both still get paid or released through title, so check the balances first and you will know your real net before you agree to a price.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
A little paperwork up front keeps a Fort Collins sale from stalling at the title stage. Pull these together before you accept an offer.

  • Your latest tax statement, or a printed receipt from the Treasurer's site showing what has been paid.
  • The parcel's tax and property record from the county search, so you can match the legal owner name and address to what title will see.
  • Payoff information from your mortgage servicer, if a loan is still open.
  • Any notice about a special assessment, since those are billed on their own pages and can be missed.
  • For a manufactured home, the separate records the Treasurer keeps for that type of property.

Owners who have been paying through mortgage escrow sometimes never see the county bill. If that is you, ask your servicer for the last statement it paid so the numbers line up with the certificate.

The tax piece moves in a predictable order whether the buyer uses a loan or pays cash. The title company opens a file, orders the Certificate of Taxes Due, and reviews it with the rest of the title search. Anything owed shows up there. If a lien is attached to the account, the title company tells you the payoff and plans to settle it from your proceeds.

Because the bill you hold covers the previous year, the current year's share is the open question at a mid-year closing. Your closing company will say how it is divided between you and the buyer, and you should read that line on the settlement statement before you sign.

After closing, the new owner updates the mailing address with the county so statements reach the right person. Sellers should do the same for any final notices, using the address change option on the Treasurer's site.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Fort Collins?
faqs.a: You pay the Larimer County Treasurer, not the city. The Treasurer collects for the school district, the city, the county and special districts.

faqs.q: When is the next Larimer County tax lien sale?
faqs.a: It is set for 8:00 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at the Larimer County Fairgrounds at the Ranch in Loveland.

faqs.q: Can I pay Fort Collins property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. You can pay two equal installments or one full payment, but partial payments are not accepted. Owners without escrow can also enroll in EquaPay for monthly payments.

faqs.q: Which office do I call if I disagree with my value?
faqs.a: Call the Larimer County Assessor. The Treasurer does not determine the amount of tax and sends value questions there.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fort Collins house that has tax due?
faqs.a: Yes. Your title company orders a Certificate of Taxes Due, and any balance is paid at closing. If the account is delinquent, call the Treasurer before the November lien sale.
